newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-HEARTS SACK PAILLE AFTER POSITIVE DOPE TEST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HEARTS SACK PAILLE AFTER POSITIVE DOPE TEST.

text.p: Scottish premier division Hearts sacked former French international striker Stephane Paille on Tuesday after he failed to random dope test.
It was the second time the 31-year-old former French Footballer of the Year had failed a dope test, and he became the first player to be caught by Scottish football's drug-testing programme.
He tested positive for an amphetamine-based medicament calledDinintel after a premier division match at Kilmarnock on April 5.
The Scottish Football Association imposed a four-month ban from July 19 to November 19 after investigating the case.
But after hearing the news, Hearts sacked him and his career is now in some jeopardy.
A Hearts spokesman said: "We are deeply disappointed in the player's actions."
The Scottish Professional Footballers' Association said Paille took the drug Dinintel to try to control a weight problem.
In September 1995 Paille failed a dope test playing a second division match in France for Mulhouse against Niort.
He had played abroad for Porto in Portugal and Servette in Switzerland and announced his retirement from the sport following the test.
But he told the sports newspaper l'Equipe at the time his retirement was due to serious personal problems and had nothing to do with the affair.
Paille came out of retirement and joined Hearts earlier this season but he was in hiding on Tuesday and expected to make a statement on Wednesday.

A statement from the Scottish Professional Footballers Association said: "Mr Paille had taken the drug Dinintel, which is an appetite suppressant, used to control weight problems. Unfortunately this contained a banned substance, contravening Regulation One of the SFA Doping Charter.
"The player states quite categorically that he did not take this drug in an effort to gain advantage on the field of play, but merely as a method of controlling his weight.

SPFA secretary Tony Higgins said: "We are devastated for Stephane in this particular case, we are convinced he only took the drug to control his weight, and certainly not as a performance-enhancing drug.
"However it is a warning to all players never to take any form of medication without consulting their Club doctor or physiotherapist."
The SFA introduced random dope testing at the start of the 1988-89 season.
